summary: Lookout station on Redding's County Offices Building, used from 1931; a new 14-foot station went up there in 1932; FFLA now lists the rooftop site as gone.

facts.design: Station 14 feet square on top of the County Offices Building (1932 report)
facts.status_note: FFLA California list marks the rooftop lookout gone; no source describes the building or station today
facts.agency: State district office under ranger W. J. Hufford

events.note: Lookout station on top of the old high school or county offices building, per a Searchlight report from May 1931
Lookouts stationed atop the county offices building spotted fires in July 1931
Two fires spotted from the building, one on Clear Creek and one in the upper Churn Creek valley, about five acres each
30-acre grass and oak timber fire near the Parkville schoolhouse on Bear Creek, reported in a Searchlight report dated July 9, 1931; located by the Redding lookout the afternoon before
New 14-foot-square station erected on the County Offices Building on Placer Street; cost $100
Thomas Boswell of Redding to be the lookout in the new station

evidence.supports: lookout located atop the county office building (Forest Lookouts heading)
state forces set up the lookout station in 1931
evidence.quote: A great improvement in the facilities of the state forces here is under way.

evidence.supports: 1931 station on top of the old high school or county offices building; Hufford's headquarters
evidence.quote: It is a lookout station on top of the old high school, or county offices building, in which Hufford has his headquarters.

evidence.supports: canvas used in 1931 to shade the lookouts from the sun; trouble when winds rose (1932 report, 'last year')
evidence.quote: Last year a canvass was used to protect the lookouts from the sun, but when winds rose difficulty was experienced.

evidence.supports: lookouts on the building spotted two fires in July 1931
evidence.quote: Lookouts stationed atop the county offices building spotted two fires, one on Clear creek, two miles west of the Pacific highway and one at the upper end of Churn Creek valley.

evidence.supports: each fire burned about five acres
evidence.quote: Five acres were burned over in each instance

evidence.supports: 30-acre fire near the Parkville schoolhouse on Bear Creek
evidence.quote: July 9, 1931: Fire burned over 30 acres of grass and oak timber near the Parkville schoolhouse on Bear creek yesterday afternoon.

evidence.supports: fire located by the Redding lookout
evidence.quote: It was located by the Redding lookout at 12:30

evidence.supports: new station erected atop the County Offices Building on Placer Street in 1932
evidence.quote: Beginning with the erection of a lookout station atop the County Offices Building on Placer street
The station on the building will be 14 feet square.
The lookout station, which has just been completed and painted, cost $100.

evidence.supports: Hufford preparing forces for the 1932 season; state district ranger
evidence.quote: W. J. Hufford, state district ranger, is lining up his forces in preparation for the 1932 fire season.

evidence.supports: Thomas Boswell of Redding to be the lookout in the new observatory
evidence.quote: Thomas Boswell of Redding will be lookout stationed in the new observatory on top of the county office building on Placer street

evidence.supports: FFLA California list marks the Redding roof top lookout gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The May 1931 report says the station sat on the old high school or the county offices building; the 1932 reports name the County Offices Building on Placer Street. The story follows the 1932 wording and flags the 1931 hedge.

sources.title: Redding
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts, quoting The Searchlight (1931-1932) and the Courier-Free Press (1932)

notes_for_editor: All historical detail comes from one page quoting 1931-32 newspapers; two web searches found no second source naming Thomas Boswell or the station. Next checks: Shasta Historical Society archive or Redding Record Searchlight files. Whether the building or station survives is unknown. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the Ron Kemnow name was dropped from the citation (the page does not name him as author), and the 1931 fire date now follows the July 9, 1931 report.
